reasons: Both answers diagnose the problem the same way, meet every rubric item, and ship nearly identical server spherecast plus client-rendered architectures. A is slightly more robust: it tells the caster to remove the predicted visual when the server rejects a cast (B leaves a ghost fireball), caps active projectiles per player, notifies clients on range fizzle, and gives concrete exploit-test steps. B's quick-fix option (SetNetworkOwner(nil), Debris) and its note about mouse.Hit aiming are useful, but they don't outweigh A's more complete handling of edge cases.
